note: Two courts and two first-round matchUps: the first Garman slot holds one matchUp per court, so both start at the venue opening.

One court, T = 90, L = 30. Periods number from 0 at the opening (period 0 totals C, period 1 adds none, as Brian Garman's published tables do), and each total is rounded to the nearest match: 1, 1, 1.33 → 1, 1.67 → 2, so the second matchUp starts at 11:30, when the first is expected to end (scheduling-pipeline.md § 9.6, decided).

Both semifinals at 10:00 on two courts; their players are free at 10:00 + 90 + 60 = 12:30, so the final, profiled the same day, takes the first slot at or after 12:30, which is 12:30 (two courts: 10:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 12:30, ...).

A DO_NOT_SCHEDULE request from 10:00 to 11:30 for a participant placed in the matchUp: a 90 minute matchUp overlaps it from any start before 11:30, so the 10:00 slot is refused and the matchUp takes the court's next slot, 11:30.
A daily limit of one singles matchUp: every finalist is already booked for a semifinal on the date, so the final is over the limit and reported as such, never timed.
The venue's only court is disabled on the date: there are no slots, and every profiled matchUp is reported without a time.

Both semifinals were played on day 2 and the final is profiled on day 1: every slot on day 1 is before its played sources, so the final is held back under the played order and not reported as merely untimed.

A standard best-of-3 matchUp (90 minutes, § 3.3) is timed at 10:00 on the only court; a round of timed SET3-S:T20/TB7 matchUps (60 minutes) is profiled. The court is held for the timed matchUp's own 90 minutes, not the profiled round's 60, so the round starts at 11:30 and 12:30.

A matchUp timed at 10:00 on the only court, and a matchUp elsewhere in the view with three draw positions. A booking reads a schedule, not draw positions: the court is still held, and the profiled matchUp starts at 11:30.
A matchUp timed at 10:00 at the venue with no court holds one of the venue's courts for its 90 minutes: the profiled matchUp on the only court starts at 11:30.
In a tournament with two venues, a matchUp timed at 10:00 with neither a venue nor a court claims no court: the profiled matchUp takes the court at 10:00 (its participants are still held, § 3.4).
In a tournament with exactly one venue, a matchUp timed at 10:00 with no venue is at that venue (CA 2026-10-25): it holds the only court until 11:30, so the profiled matchUp is timed at 11:30.

A BYE carries a schedule (10:00 on day 2) and the final is profiled on day 2 under a daily limit of one singles matchUp. A BYE is never played: it adds nothing to its participant's day and raises no not-before time, so the final is timed at 10:00, not held over the limit.

The short-format semifinals (SET1-S:6/TB7: 30 minutes, 30 recovery) are timed at 10:00; a 90 minute round of another event is profiled at the same venue, with the final. A stored matchUp holds its participants for its own minutes (CA 2026-10-25), not the venue's greatest average: the finalists are free at 11:00.

Short-format semifinals and their final (SET1-S:6/TB7: 30 minutes, 30 recovery) are profiled with a 90 minute round of another event at the same venue. A placed matchUp holds its participants for its round's own average (CA 2026-10-25), the figure its recovery is checked with, not the venue's greatest.

A DO_NOT_SCHEDULE request from 10:45 for a participant of a short-format semifinal (30 minutes), profiled with a 90 minute round at the same venue. The request is checked against the matchUp's own minutes (CA 2026-10-25): 10:00 to 10:30 does not reach it, so the semifinal is timed at 10:00.

A first-round matchUp timed at 18:00 on day 1 is profiled again on day 2 with the final. It is placed at 10:00, and its targets wait only for where it is placed now (CA 2026-10-25): its day-1 recovery end (20:30) is no not-before time.

Two venues (6 courts and 1) share one field of 16 players across two draws, their rounds profiled at both. A venue's turn ends once it has placed as many matchUps as it has courts open on the date (CA 2026-10-25); it ran to one more, counting every court of the venue. The turns decide which venue reaches a shared player first: 17 matchUps are timed, not 16.

A matchUp timed at 19:00 at the venue with no court runs 90 minutes, past the courts' 20:00 close: no court's free time ends around it, so it holds none, and the plan reports it under unbookedMatchUpIds rather than dropping it (§ 3.9 rule 4).

The semifinals (30 minutes, 30 recovery) end at 10:30 at one venue; the final is profiled at another, 60 minutes away. Recovery counts toward transit, so the finalists are free at the greater: 10:30 + 60 = 11:30 (CA 2026-10-25).
The same, 15 minutes away: recovery (to 11:00) is the greater, and transit adds nothing.
No minutes stated for the pair: the default (60) applies, so the final is at 11:30.
The two venues share a facility: one physical place, no transit, whatever the default (60). The final is at 11:00.
A one-way value from the second venue back to the first (60), none the other way and no default: going from the first venue to the second takes no transit, so the final is at 11:00.
The attached scheduling policy states defaultTimes.transitMinutes of 60: the view reads it as the default for a pair with no stated minutes, and the final is at 11:30.

Two events profiled on the first date (a Monday). The first plays Tuesdays only (event weekdays), so its round is skipped on the Monday: the view gives it no matchUps and no minutes, and nothing of it is timed (§ 4, step 2). The second event plays every day and is timed as though the first were not profiled. Skipping is per event, by the round's event.
As the case before, with the call's allowInactiveEventDates: the round of the event that does not play on the date is planned like any other, and a run warns about each placement it makes.

A matchUp stored at 23:00 on the first date runs past midnight, but the call clears the first date, which it plans: what is stored there is gone and carries no court into the next date (§ 9.8). On the second date the court opens at 00:00 and the profiled matchUp is timed then, not at 00:30.

A junior first-round matchUp is timed at 21:00 on the first date (90 minutes: play ends 22:30). The default policy's overnight rest for JUNIOR is 12 hours, which a player may waive: it is warned, not held (§ 9.8, CA 2026-10-25). Recovery alone ends the night before, so the final takes the first slot of the next date, 08:00.
